question_and_gold.question: What was the date when the document authorizing the annexation of the former Captaincy General of Guatemala into the First Mexican Empire was signed by the individual who held the office that governed from the Palacio de los Capitanes Generales, an office established after the colonization began in 1524, and which first implemented the provincial division decreed by the Cádiz Cortes in 1812?

evidence.exact_quote: The Consultive Junta of Guatemala City was the Central American government at the time, not the Captain General.
The document states that the request for annexation was accepted on 5 January 1822.
The document authorizing annexation was the decision/vote of the Consultive Junta, signed/led by Gaínza.
The junta was led by Guatemalan General Gabino Gaínza.
The vote itself constitutes the authorization. Gaínza was the head of the Junta.
The Captaincy General of Guatemala was governed from the Palacio de los Capitanes Generales (also known as the Captain General Palace) in Antigua Guatemala.
Two days after that date, Gaínza Fernandez de Medrano was able to send his response
